create.name: Thupten Jinpa
create.bio:
Thupten Jinpa is a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher of compassion who has served as the Dalai Lama's chief English translator since 1985, travelling with him across North America and Europe. He trained in the classical Tibetan monastic system, where he earned the Geshe Lharam, the highest degree of that curriculum, and went on to study philosophy and then religious studies at the University of Cambridge, finishing with a doctorate.

Alongside translating and editing many of the Dalai Lama's books, he founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics in Montreal, which is bringing key texts of Tibetan thought into modern languages, and he leads it as president and editor-in-chief. He is also the founder of the Compassion Institute and chairs the Mind and Life Institute, which brings contemplative practice into dialogue with science. He was the principal author of Compassion Cultivation Training, a structured programme for learning compassion first developed at Stanford University and now taught by certified teachers around the world.

His book A Fearless Heart explains how compassion can be trained like a muscle and become a source of inner strength. He has also written Tsongkhapa, a biography of a founding figure of the Gelug school, and he teaches through online courses, talks and conversations with the Compassion Institute.

books.title: A Fearless Heart: How the Courage to Be Compassionate Can Transform Our Lives
books.author: Thupten Jinpa
books.description: Jinpa sets out how compassion works as an inner resource that can be strengthened through practice, drawing on Buddhist training and on the course he helped design at Stanford.

books.title: Tsongkhapa: A Buddha in the Land of Snows
books.author: Thupten Jinpa
books.description: A full-length biography of Tsongkhapa, the Tibetan master behind the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, drawn from Tibetan sources.
